rationale: Bound the completed ballot-progress receipt into the authority question: two ordinary owner-side recovery attempts repeat the identical rejected prepare and dispatch nothing, while the same attempt after the target's own BeTheLeader authority climbs and completes the instance. The question's discrimination is answered (no repair without the designated authority), so its disposition is set to explained, and the two supporting behaviors now cite the executed indices.

knowledge.statement: In handlePrepareReply a reply whose Ballot differs from lb.lastTriedBallot increments lb.nacks and returns before the reply is appended to lb.prepareReplies, and the sub-case dispatch is guarded by len(lb.prepareReplies) >= SlowQuorumSize(); the only repair on the nack path (makeBallot plus a fresh bcastPrepare) is executed only while r.IsLeader is true. When every answering peer reports a higher stored ballot, the appended count stays at the recovering replica's own self reply, so no sub-case is selected and no PreAccept, Accept or Commit is emitted for that instance.
knowledge.conditions: Recovery where the replicas that answer the Prepare have a stored bal above the recovering replica's fixed tried ballot, so every answer is a rejection rather than a matching-ballot reply (epaxos/epaxos.go:1204-1235, with epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451 and 1216-1235).

knowledge.statement: makeBallot assigns the instance owner the ballot equal to its own replica id and any other recovering replica id+N, and advances it in steps of N only while r.IsLeader is true and the candidate is below maxRecvBallot; epaxos.New hardcodes IsLeader false and only the exported BeTheLeader RPC sets it, which the master invokes for the replica it designates. Repeating startRecoveryForInstance without that flag therefore reuses the identical ballot, whereas after the flag is set the same call emits a ballot above maxRecvBallot.
knowledge.conditions: Any startRecoveryForInstance call in the captured snapshot, including repeat calls from executeCommands after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451, 1127-1150, 149-165, 1121-1125).

interpretations.rationale: Current account: in the captured EPaxos package the ability to recover an instance whose stored ballot is above the recovering replica's own ballot depends on the master-designated IsLeader flag; without it the replica's retry repeats an identical rejected prepare and the recovery dispatches nothing at all. Witnesses from receipt 911d45335b3047178a6fd739f24b2cfb (fixed experiment adfa9c6d31ca481896e5ca1277f6cdf4-experiment, test TestAssuranceEPaxosRecoveryBallotProgress, 36 parsed events, no parsing errors): events 0-2 establish the premise that the owner's pre-accept replies were not equal (acceptor 1 answered with status PREACCEPTED while acceptor 2 answered PREACCEPTED_EQ), leaving owner replica 0 with status ACCEPTED and cmd_op 1; event 3 shows the owner's Accept broadcast at ballot 0 to replicas 1 and 2, and events 4-5 show those replicas recording the accepted coordinates at bal 0 with cmd_op 1. Events 6-10 show replica 2 recovering the same instance at its own ballot 7; events 11-14 show replicas 0, 1, 3 and 4 joining that ballot (bal 7) without any accepted value at 7, and replica 2 was failed before consuming the replies, so the instance stayed uncommitted while the quorum's stored ballot was 7. Event 16 records the owner's first recovery round with is_leader false and max_recv_ballot 7; events 17-19 are the three peer replies, each carrying Ballot 7 while the owner tried ballot 0, so all three were rejections; event 20 is the decisive result: tried_ballot 0, prepare_ballots [0,0,0], stored_bal_before_attempt 7, prepare_ballot_above_stored_bal false, appended_replies 1 against slow_quorum 3, subcase_dispatched false, follow_up [] and instance_status 3 - the recovery emitted nothing and the instance stayed accepted but uncommitted. Events 21-25 repeat the same attempt through the executor's retry path with identical operands (tried_ballot 0, the same three Ballot-7 replies, appended_replies 1, no follow-up), which satisfies the repeated-nonprogress condition rather than a single artificial timeout. Event 26 is the target's own authority transition (BeTheLeader handler, is_leader true); event 27 starts round 3 with max_recv_ballot 7, events 28-30 show the peers joining the climbed ballot 10 and answering with matching Ballot 10, event 31 shows appended_replies 3 >= slow_quorum 3, subcase_dispatched true and follow_up [accept, accept], and event 32 shows the owner COMMITTED with cmd_op 1 (X preserved), with events 33-35 recording the same committed value at replicas 1, 3 and 4. Declared comparisons: 0 and 1 are violated with complete witnesses 20 and 25 (the retarded attempts neither dispatch a sub-case nor use a ballot above the stored one), and the control comparisons 2 and 3 hold (evaluated indices 31 and 32). The scoped defect is therefore the authority gate itself: the ballot that can act on an instance whose stored ballot is higher is only acquirable with the master-designated IsLeader flag, so an ordinary replica - here the instance owner, whose fixed ballot is its own id - cannot recover such an instance and emits no follow-up of any kind.
counterevidence: The blocker is a peer-side stored ballot left by a failed recovery coordinator; it is not a general inability to recover. An updated client retry or another replica that knows the instance can still act: replicas with a fixed ballot above the stored one (id+N > 7, i.e. replicas 3 and 4 with ballots 8 and 9) would not be rejected by this mechanism, and the designated-leader control in this very receipt shows the recovery completing with the accepted value X.

The peers' answers in rounds 1 and 2 are legitimate protocol behaviour, not a fault: each reports the ballot it stored (7) and the recovering replica's 0 was genuinely below it, so the rejection does not by itself demonstrate a violation of the peer's duty.
The defect requires the higher-ballot record to pre-exist; in this run it came from a recovery attempt that failed after broadcasting its Prepare, which is a permitted failure but a specific one.

Because handlePrepare does not advance crtInstance, replicas 3 and 4 knew of instance (0,0) only as a placeholder after the ballot-7 Prepare and would not have been triggered by their own executors in this run, so no other replica attempted the instance here; the claim therefore rests on the retry behaviour of the replica that ran the recovery, not on a measured statement about every replica in the system.
limitations: One configuration and one extreme case: N=5, F=2, instance (0,0), and the recoverer is the instance owner, whose fixed ballot is 0, the lowest possible; the same mechanism was not exercised for a non-owner recoverer (id+N) or for a stored ballot between the two.

The harness delivered the owner's Prepare and the peers' rejections explicitly and re-invoked startRecoveryForInstance instead of waiting for the executor's COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD retry (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417 was not run), so the retry cadence is modelled, not measured.

The premise state (peers storing bal 7 with an uncommitted instance) was produced by failing replica 2 after its Prepare broadcast and discarding its replies; the harness schedules that delivery rather than relying on real transport timing.

The authority in the control comparison came from invoking the target's own BeTheLeader handler directly; the master's designation policy, its reassignment after a replica is detected dead, and the case of a live but non-designated replica were not exercised.
No client is present: the claim concerns the recovery attempt's messages and the instance's state, not a measured client-visible latency or completion interval.
interpretations.joint_history: Producer and result events all belong to receipt 911d45335b3047178a6fd739f24b2cfb for fixed experiment adfa9c6d31ca481896e5ca1277f6cdf4-experiment and describe the same instance (0,0): events 0-5 are the owner's proposal and Accept phase, events 6-14 the failed higher-ballot recovery and the peers' stored ballot, events 16-25 the two blocked owner-side attempts, and events 26-35 the authority control and its outcome.
